style: Lively and friendly, like the dispatcher at a busy painting company calling out the day's jobs.
lines: Calls are on the board. Tap crew cards to put them on the job, then type their rate sum as one fraction.
Tap a second crew card. Then combine the rates in the box.
Add the rates, not the hours. Each card says what part of a house that crew paints in an hour. Type the total in the box.
Type an equation for one complete house, then press Check equation. Use the variable named on the call.
Type the time, then press Check time. You can press Paint to test a positive time estimate on the house.
Type both possible brush times, separated by a comma. Press Check roots, then judge each one.
Mark each root and pick a reason. Type the sprayer times for those roots, in order, separated by a semicolon. Then press Check fit.
Press Paint to test your checked calculation on the house. You can change crews or calls at any time.
Type the time and total cost. Choose whether this crew meets the deadline, then press Check quote.
All three pairs are tested. Choose the cheapest crew that meets the deadline and type its total cost.
Job done, right on time.
House complete, but this crew misses the three hour deadline. Try another pair.
Tap crew cards to assign another pair. Your tested quotes stay on the ledger.
Fill the two boxes to write the time as 4 minus something. Then drag the x slider.
Use the remainder form to answer both questions, then press Check reasoning.
Mark each root and type its evidence. Press File audit. Check in the original shows a worked example with no credit.
Type a zero denominator or the equal value of both sides for each root; use ; between roots. Press File audit.
Choose another sheet, or change a verdict and press File audit.
Choose another call with the call picker, or open Quote sheet.
Caught it. That value breaks the equation.
